title: Harm or Humor: A Multimodal, Multilingual Benchmark for Overt and Covert Harmful Humor

bias_targets.methodology: Comparing the performance of LLMs and VLMs on harmful humor detection between English and Arabic datasets, revealing a sharp 'English bias' where models systematically degrade when processing Arabic text, image, and video data.

Evaluating models on their ability to recognize implicit harmful humor that relies on locally defined, culturally specific cues and contextual reasoning, demonstrating that current models struggle to generalize safety guardrails beyond Western/English cultural norms.

Analyzing the tendency of certain open-source vision-language models to exhibit a severe 'safe bias,' where aggressive safety alignment causes the model to default to predicting 'safe' or yielding refusal-like outputs instead of properly detecting harmful humor.

Testing models on a benchmark of jokes categorized as 'Harmful' based on their use of sensitive demographic themes (e.g., racism, sexuality, disability, religion) to demean or target individuals, evaluated in aggregate across explicit and implicit harm types.
